subject: Compute partial correlations in generated quantities?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Compute partial correlations in generated quantities?
parts:
Hi folks,

Ben previously enumerated various definitions of partial correlation (https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/Xw3RTxH4zG8/e_2KFMFeBQAJ) and I'd like to compute the first variant in the generated quantities section of my model. However I'm not clear on how to "invert the covariance matrix, rescale it to a correlation matrix, and negate the off-diagonal elements". Help?

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compute partial correlations in generated quantities?
parts:
The hard part is the rescaling which
relates the correlation matrix Omega, the covariance
matrix Sigma and the scale vector sigma:

Sigma = diag_matrix(sigma) * Omega * diag_matrix(sigma)

so you can solve the other way as:

Omega[i, j] = Sigma[i, j] / ( sigma[i] * sigma[j])

with

sigma[i] = sqrt(Sigma[i, i])Sigma = diag_matrix(sigma) *

I'll write up a section on this relation for the next manual
release:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2051#issuecomment-257343482

- Bob

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compute partial correlations in generated quantities?
parts:
Thanks for the response Bob! So, given the following multivariate model, would the generated quantities section at the end be correctly producing the partial correlations (of Ben's first definition)?


  data {
    # N: number of cases
    int<lower=1> N ;
    #: K: number of outcome variables
    int K ;
    # Y: matrix of outcomes for each case & variable
    matrix[N,K] Y ; 
  }
  parameters {
    # means: vector of population-level means per variable
    vector[K] means ; 
    # sds: vector of population-level sds per variable
    vector<lower=0>[K] sds ;
    # cor: population-level correlations amongst variables
    corr_matrix[K] cor ;
  }
  transformed parameters{
    # cov: covariance matrix (derived from cor & sds)
    matrix[K,K] cov ; 
    #compute covariance matrix from cor & sds
    cov = quad_form_diag(cor,sds) ;
  }
  model {
    #priors on population parameters; presumes data has been scale()ed 
    means ~ normal(0,1) ;
    sds ~ lognormal(0,1) ;
    cor ~ lkj_corr(1) ; 
    #assert sampling of case-level outcomes on each variable given 
    #  multivariate normal population
    for(s in 1:N){
      Y[s,] ~ multi_normal(means,cov) ;
    }
  }
  generated quantities{
    # pcor: partial correlation matrix
    matrix[K,K] pcor ;
    # icov: inverse of covariance matrix
    matrix[K,K] icov ;
    # svec: scale vector for conversion of icov to correlation matrix
    vector[K] svec ;
    #compute inverse of covariance
    icov = 1/cov ;
    #compute scale vactor
    for(i in 1:K){
      svec[i] = sqrt(icov[i,i]) ;
    }
    #convert inverse covariance matrix to a partial correlation matrix
    for(i in 1:K){
      for(j in 1:K){
        pcor[i, j] = icov[i, j] / (svec[i] * svec[j])
        #negate off-diagonal
        if(i!=j){
          pcor[i, j] = -pcor[i, j]
        }
      }
    }
  }

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compute partial correlations in generated quantities?
parts:
What I was proposing was computing the correlation matrix, and
I now realize you're talking about partial correlations, which
is what we use to build up the correlation matrix.

That's much trickier to factor. The transform and its inverse
are in the chapter in the manual on "Transformations of Constrained
Variables".

I also didn't get the negation bit in what you're doing --- if it
is a correlation matrix, it should be symmetric, not negated.

- Bob
